fixes.why: The label says nothing the verses share, and none of its four examples prints heart in the Berean: Gen 31:20 is “Jacob deceived Laban the Aramean”, Exod 14:5 “changed their minds”, Num 16:28 “it was not my own doing”, Dan 4:16 “the mind of a beast” (checked in the Berean API for Gen 31:20). A reader checking the English cannot see why these are in a heart hub, which breaks rule 6.
fixes.fix: Relabel to what the verses share, for example 'Where the Berean prints mind, deceit or another word for the Hebrew heart', and show each example's Hebrew word beside its English; if no such label is accurate, dissolve the row and place each verse under the row it fits.

fixes.row: The LORD, God, searches, tests and knows the heart
fixes.why: These verses carry the Hebrew word for kidneys (כִּלְיָה), which the hub's own 'Other words translated heart' section names apart (Ps 7:9, Ps 26:2, Jer 11:20, Jer 20:12, Ps 73:21 are listed there under kidneys). Ps 7:9 reads “searches hearts and minds” and Jer 11:20 “examines the heart and mind”, where the Berean's heart is the kidneys. The row's rule 4 (never equate two different original words) is broken by its own membership, even though its note says the page does not make them one. Ps 73:21 also sits in 'Troubled, broken, faint or afraid'.
fixes.fix: Move Ps 7:9, Ps 26:2, Jer 11:20 and Jer 20:12 out of this row so they appear only under 'Other words translated heart' as kidneys; move Ps 73:21 out of the 'Troubled' row the same way.

fixes.row: In believers' hearts: the Spirit, Christ, the peace of God; cleansed by faith
fixes.why: Rom 2:29 reads “a man is a Jew because he is one inwardly, and circumcision is a matter of the heart, by the Spirit, not by the written code” (checked in the Berean API). It is Paul's statement about who is a Jew and about the written code, not about believers, and the row's heading files it under believers as if the text said so. The rabbi would object to a Christian heading placed over a verse about Israel without saying so.
fixes.fix: Keep the verse but rewrite the note sentence so it says whom the verse is about: 'Rom 2:29 says who is a Jew inwardly, and that circumcision is of the heart by the Spirit; it speaks of the Jew and of the written code, and the page takes no side on how Paul's words apply to believers.' Delete the row-10 claim that it describes believers.

fixes.why: The note quotes Judg 19:22 as “While they were enjoying themselves”, which is the Berean's opening clause. The verse continues: “the wicked men of the city surrounded the house ... so we can have relations with him!” (checked in the Berean API). It is a mob scene threatening sexual violence against a guest, and setting its opening words under joy softens the text, against rule 1.
fixes.fix: Remove Judg.19.22 from this row and delete the note's sentence about it. If the Hebrew 'making their hearts glad' is to be shown, place the verse under 'Every other use' with the Berean's full sentence beside it, not the opening clause.

fixes.row: What a person does with the heart, or is told to do: set, prepare, turn, guard, give, circumcise, make new
fixes.why: The note says “The row above has the heart as it is; the row below what God does.” That reads as a sequence, heart as it is, then human turning, then God's work, which the no-ranking sentence and the alphabetical order deny. The row above is 'Pure, clean ...', not 'the heart as it is'. On prevenient grace a sequence leans toward an answer, which the page is meant not to give.
fixes.fix: Delete that sentence from the note. The row labels already say what each row holds.

fixes.why: The note quotes Dan 7:28 as “I kept the matter in my heart”. The Berean prints “But I kept the matter to myself.” (checked in the Berean API), and the example shows no heart. The Aramaic does read 'in my heart', but the note presents that as the English.
fixes.fix: Quote the Berean (“But I kept the matter to myself.”) and add: 'The Aramaic reads “in my heart”; the Berean does not print heart.'

fixes.why: The note says “The Berean prints ‘heart’ at 1 John 3:17 (‘withholds his compassion’)”. The Berean prints “withholds his compassion from him” and no heart (checked in the Berean API). The note contradicts its own example.
fixes.fix: Replace with: 'The Berean prints “compassion” at 1 John 3:17; the Greek is σπλάγχνα, the inward parts, the seat of pity.'

fixes.row: Other words translated “heart” (kidneys, inner parts, belly, soul)
fixes.why: The section is titled 'Other words translated heart', but the Berean does not print heart in these examples: Ps 5:9 “destruction lies within them” (קֶרֶב), Job 32:19 “my belly is like unvented wine” and Prov 22:18 “within you” (בֶּטֶן), Gen 34:8 “longs for your daughter” (נֶפֶשׁ), Ps 55:15 “evil is with them in their homes” (קֶרֶב). Only the interlinear gloss says heart. Rule 6 and the section's own title are not met for these items (the first four were checked in the Berean API).
fixes.fix: Drop these items from the section, or move them to a plain list of other Hebrew words for inward parts that the Berean does not render as heart. Keep in the section only words whose Berean verses print heart or a note giving the Hebrew, such as Ps 10:3 and Ps 40:8.

worker_points.point: 1. How far sin reaches in the heart (total depravity) and whether God's work comes before turning (prevenient grace): five rows, one no-side sentence each, alphabetical, 'carry no ranking'.
worker_points.why: The substance is balanced and each row carries the same no-side sentence, and the rows are in alphabetical order. But the note under 'What a person does' sets a sequence ('the row above ... the row below'), which contradicts the ranking disclaimer.

worker_points.point: 2. The three searcher rows: the LORD named; Jesus named or His own 'I'; 'the Lord' or 'He' with no name.
worker_points.why: Each row's doors match what its verses name, and the note gives the readings of 'the Lord' without choosing. Reformed, Lutheran, Catholic and Eastern Orthodox readers can accept the split. Only the kidney verses in the first row need moving (see fixes).

worker_points.point: 3. Row 'The heart of God, and of Jesus' (grieved, regret, 'after My own heart', 'gentle and humble in heart').
worker_points.why: The verses are the text's own words and the note says the page does not say how literally they are taken. Wesleyan, Baptist and Eastern Orthodox readers can accept it as set down.

worker_points.point: 4. Pronoun-only verses ('He' or 'You' in a prayer whose passage names the LORD) inside 'What God does to the heart'.
worker_points.why: The passages name the LORD in context and the note lists each verse. The stricter rule the worker offers is not needed for this panel.

worker_points.point: 5. Heart as mind and will, not only feeling (rows on willing, wisdom, thinking).
worker_points.why: The verses support it (Ps 14:1, Prov 16:9, Luke 2:19, Exod 35:21) and the notes say so in the text's words.

worker_points.point: 6. Human skill: the craftsmen 'wise of heart' (Exod 28:3, 31:6, 35:10 and others) placed under wisdom with a note.
worker_points.why: The note says it is skill given to the craftsmen, not the wisdom of Proverbs 8, which is accurate and keeps the Hebrew Scriptures on their own terms.

worker_points.point: 7. Hard verses kept: Heb 3:12, Isa 6:10, Isa 63:17, Rom 1:24, Rev 17:17, Ps 105:25, Prov 22:15, Ps 73:13, John 13:2, Acts 5:3.
worker_points.why: Each is the text's own statement and is set under a row whose label fits it. None is softened and none is given a verdict.

examples_checked: 23 of 24 rows' examples show their label; the row 'Every other use' shows no heart in its four examples; 12 verses checked in the Berean API
summary: The hub is faithful in its large rows and its contested block is balanced with no verdict and no ranking, and I found no US political framing. It still has a misquote of Dan 7:28, a note that says the Berean prints heart where it does not (1 John 3:17), a softened mob scene (Judg 19:22), kidney-word verses in the searching row, a row whose examples show no heart, and an 'other words' section with items the Berean does not translate heart; all are fixable, so ship after fixes.
